town.name: Kottur
town.description: Largest panchayat town in the Pollachi-Anaimalai belt, 15 km west of Pollachi, at the foot of the Western Ghats on the Kerala border, beside the Parambikulam and Anamalai Tiger Reserve corridor. Flood prone, low infrastructure.
town.context: Monsoon flood + landslide at km 42 of the ghat road (the Pollachi-Valparai road). Fuel depot cut off, hospital on generator, water pump dead, 200 people in three shelters with no water.
town.scope_note: Kottur is the reference town, not a special case. The organ graph, the A* road search and the allocator are parameterised by town.json, so any low-infrastructure town with a fuel reserve, a hospital, a pump and shelters runs the same cascade.

global.people_in_scope: ~3.5 billion people live in low-infrastructure, flood-exposed regions
global.pattern: fuel depot = blood, hospital = heart, water pump = lungs, shelters = organs
global.why_it_transfers: The organ graph is data. Any blocked road becomes a new edge weight; the same A* search, the same topological order, the same constrained allocation runs unchanged.
global.evidence_note: 3.5B is an order-of-magnitude figure for people in low- and middle-income countries exposed to flood risk; cite the source in the submission form.

crisis.summary: Landslide at km 42 of the ghat road closes the 4.2 km direct corridor for ~6 h. The depot holds 100 L diesel. Hospital generator has 4 h of runtime left. The water pump is fed from the hospital feeder and 200 people in shelters have no water.

allocation_policy.rule: Hospital first (lives at immediate risk), pump second (200 people's water), shelters follow the pump. Never allocate more than a node's stated demand. Total must equal the reserve exactly.
allocation_policy.no_medical_advice: This agent allocates diesel only. It never triages patients, doses medicine, or gives clinical advice.

road_network.notes: Road lengths are surveyed corridor lengths (km), coordinates are WGS84 waypoints used only for the A* heuristic. The signposted detour without an agent is the 13.0 km Kottur bypass (fuel_depot -> south_jn -> bypass_jn -> hospital).

baseline.metric_definition: Water-pump uptime measured during the first 4 h of the incident, and diesel burned per litre delivered.
baseline.why_uptime_improves: The naive split gives the pump 50 L but the hospital generator browns out and the feeder drops, so the pump only runs 30 min. Meeting the hospital's 70 L demand first keeps the feeder stable and the pump runs 90 min on its 30 L.

tavily.role: search, extract, map, crawl, images, answers

cascade.note: downstream failures are structural, not estimates

route.evidence: road lengths and blocked status are surveyed fields in town.json; the path is computed, not generated

snake_boat_relay.note: road A* won at 7.8 km; the water leg stayed armed and unused

ant_pheromone.note: Seeded ACO on the road graph. The blocked corridor cannot be reinforced, so its trail evaporates while the open path hardens. No randomness escapes: seed 7 reproduces every number.

sweat.folklore_verdict: not supported by the expansion coefficient
sweat.note: Volume correction only. Expansion does not spill diesel; it means the tank holds less mass per litre when it is hot. Evaporation in a sealed tank is a separate, much smaller loss and is not claimed here.

dna.algorithm: sha256 over a canonical JSON payload, chained by prev
dna.note: A hash chain makes the record append-only: changing any past lot breaks every hash after it. It is not a blockchain and this repo does not claim one - there is no network, no token and no consensus.

clock.note: Fuel-limited runtime, not a failure prediction. Mechanical failure, fuel contamination and overload tripping all shorten this and are not modelled - because no failure-sound dataset exists in this repo.

inverse.note: Runtime is fuel divided by the documented burn rate. The 90-minute figure in town.json baseline is measured pump uptime in the first four hours at duty cycle, which is a different metric and is not used here.

honesty: sweat: volume correction with a published coefficient, not evaporation

inverse: the same numbers expressed in hours

allocation.justification: Heart first, lungs next: the hospital's 4 h of runtime is the nearest failure, and the pump is fed from the hospital feeder, so 70 L hospital + 30 L pump is the only split that keeps both alive for the 6 h closure.

brain.justification: Hospital requires 70 L to cover the 6-hour road closure (E2) and has only 4 hours of generator runtime left (E1), making it the top priority (E6). Water pump needs 30 L to maintain water supply for 200 shelter residents (E3, E5) but depends on the hospital feeder for power (E6). The total reserve is 100 L (E7) and caps match exactly (hospital 70 L, water_pump 30 L), allowing full allocation without shortfall. Landslide clearance takes ~6 hours (E8, S1), confirming the demand window.
brain.note: the most recent run on this machine used the offline policy; this is the newest validated Nemotron 3 run, replayed from its artefact
